title: Pages for an allocation
description:
The operating system hands out memory in whole pages. Asking for even one byte costs a full page.

Write `pagesNeeded(bytes, pageSize)`, the number of pages needed to hold `bytes` bytes, and `roundUpToPage(bytes, pageSize)`, the number of bytes that is actually reserved.

```
pagesNeeded(1, 4096)      = 1
pagesNeeded(4096, 4096)   = 1
pagesNeeded(4097, 4096)   = 2
roundUpToPage(5000, 4096) = 8192
```

Zero bytes need zero pages. Use whole-number arithmetic only: no floating point and no `ceil`.
hints: Integer division rounds down: `4097 / 4096` is 1. You need it to round up.
Adding `pageSize - 1` before dividing pushes any leftover bytes over into the next page, without changing a size that was already exact.
rules: Use whole-number arithmetic: adding pageSize - 1 before dividing rounds up.
lessonTitle: What the Operating System Does for a Program

rules.message: Use whole-number arithmetic: adding pageSize - 1 before dividing rounds up.
